I will keep my land mostly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what I know best, it fits my well irrigation, and on 4.1 mu I need a steady grain harvest with work I can still manage at my age. I will put 3.1 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will leave 1.0 mu for cotton because I have long experience with it and I still want some cash crop income, but I will not expand it because cotton needs more careful field work and picking. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a medium level, irrigate a few key times, and use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed for stable yield, keep fertilizer balanced but not too heavy, irrigate mainly at the important growth stages, and continue with rotary tillage for convenience. For cotton, I will also stay moderate on fertilizer and water, control pests a bit more closely than grain crops, and keep the area small so I can handle it with my household labor. I am not chasing the highest possible yield; I am choosing a plan that is familiar, manageable, and dependable for my age, land size, and irrigation conditions.
